prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.62
  gal: 0.38
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key proposals (max 500 words)

Economic and fiscal policy
- Maintain strict fiscal rules: balance day-to-day spending and have debt falling by year five; all major fiscal events audited by the OBR.
- No rises to National Insurance, Income Tax rates, or VAT; reform taxation by abolishing non-domiciled status, closing carried-interest loopholes, tightening HMRC enforcement and anti-avoidance rules.
- Publish a multi-year business tax roadmap; cap corporation tax at 25%; retain full expensing and the Annual Investment Allowance; replace business rates in England.
- Create a National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private investment in ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture and green hydrogen.
- Reform pensions to boost returns and UK investment; review the pensions landscape.
- Ten-year infrastructure strategy; new National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; accelerate major projects and grid upgrades.
- Planning reform to enable labs, data centres, gigafactories; full gigabit and national 5G by 2030.

Energy, climate, and environment
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine energy, long-duration storage.
- Support nuclear (extend existing, deliver Hinkley Point C, Sizewell C, SMRs); maintain a strategic gas reserve but no new oil and gas exploration licences; ban fracking and new coal.
- Establish a publicly owned clean energy company (Great British Energy, £8.3bn) and a Local Power Plan.
- Close windfall tax loopholes and extend/raise the levy on oil and gas profits.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; minimum PRS efficiency by 2030.
- Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism; require credible net-zero transition plans for major financial institutions and FTSE 100 firms.
- Stronger water regulation, automatic fines, and executive bonus blocks for pollution; expand habitats, forests, and access to nature.
- Support for farmers; target 50% public-sector food to be local or higher-standard; improve animal welfare (e.g., trophy import ban, end puppy smuggling, snare traps).

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee with thousands of additional officers and PCSOs; tougher action on antisocial behaviour and shopworker assaults.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory interventions, curfews/tagging for serious cases; ban zombie-style blades; executive liability for illegal online sales.
- Specialist rape units in all forces; fast-track rape cases; domestic abuse experts in 999 control rooms; new offence of criminal exploitation of children.
- Police standards: mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; improved tech and fraud strategy.
- Build new prison places; reduce reoffending via work, housing, and probation reform; review sentencing.
- Address historical injustices (e.g., Hillsborough-style duty of candour; implement major inquiry findings).

Immigration and borders
- New Border Security Command with counter-terror style powers; EU security co-operation; more caseworkers; new returns unit; negotiate returns deals.
- Reform points-based system; link migration to domestic skills plans; bar rule-breaking employers.

Housing and local growth
- Build 1.5m homes over the parliament; restore mandatory housing targets; brownfield-first, strategic “grey belt” releases with safeguards; new towns.
- Boost affordable/social housing; first-refusal for local first-time buyers; permanent mortgage guarantee scheme.
- Devolution: wider powers over transport, skills, housing; multi-year council funding; statutory Local Growth Plans.

Work, education, and skills
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero-hours and fire-and-rehire; day-one rights to sick pay, parental leave, unfair dismissal protection; Single Enforcement Body; align minimum wage with cost of living and remove age bands.
- 6,500 new teachers; curriculum and assessment review; report-card inspections; reinstate support staff negotiating body; school mental health professionals.
- Free breakfast clubs in every primary; 3,000 school-based nurseries; review parental leave.
- Youth guarantee (18–21) of training, apprenticeship or job support; create Skills England; transform FE into Technical Excellence Colleges; replace Apprenticeship Levy with a flexible Growth and Skills Levy.
- Private rented sector reform: abolish Section 21, strengthen standards, tackle building safety; leasehold to be replaced by commonhold.

Health and social care
- Cut waiting lists with 2m extra operations/scans/appointments annually; shared waiting lists; use independent sector capacity; implement workforce plans.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; faster innovation adoption; enhanced NHS app functionality.
- Primary care: more GPs; guaranteed face-to-face on request; continuity incentives; pharmacist prescribing; neighbourhood health centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing for 3–5-year-olds.
- National Care Service with national standards; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care.
- 8,500 additional mental health staff; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; restrict youth-targeted vape marketing; ban junk food ads to children and high-caffeine energy drinks for under-16s; strengthen online safety; modernise gambling regulation.

Governance and democracy
- Independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; empower Ministerial Ethics Adviser; curb second jobs that conflict with duties.
- Immediate House of Lords reforms (end hereditary peers, retirement at 80, participation requirements) and consult on full replacement; votes at 16; improve voter registration/ID consistency.
- Reset intergovernmental relations; Council of the Nations and Regions; uphold devolved settlements.

Foreign, defence, and development
- Strategic Defence Review; unshakeable NATO commitment and nuclear deterrent; defence industrial strategy; support for Ukraine (including use of frozen assets).
- Improve EU relations without rejoining single market/customs union; pursue trade deals and MRAs; security pact with the EU.
- AUKUS support; calibrated China strategy; defend Overseas Territories.
- Lead a Clean Power Alliance; restore development capability; aim to return to 0.7% ODA when fiscal conditions allow.

TEXT_D:
This manifesto sets out proposals across immigration, public spending, taxation, public services, energy, policing, justice, education, welfare, Brexit, defence, housing, families, infrastructure, agriculture, fisheries, pensions/social care, constitutional change, and governance, with associated costings and savings.

Core pledges:
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; detain and remove illegal arrivals; new immigration department; offshore processing; restrict student dependants; 5‑year residency for benefits; higher employer NI (20%) for foreign workers with exemptions.
- Zero NHS waiting lists by using independent capacity, tax incentives for staff, vouchers when waiting times exceed set limits, and efficiency reforms.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; scrap energy levies and VAT on energy; expand domestic oil and gas.
- Reduce government waste via departmental efficiency (5%), ending interest on QE reserves, halving foreign aid, improving tax collection, and deregulation.

Tax and economy:
- Personal: Lift income tax start point to £20k; higher rate from £70k; cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap energy levies and VAT on bills; cut stamp duty (0% under £750k, 2% to £1.5m, 4% above); restore VAT‑free tourist shopping; reform inheritance tax (no IHT under £2m; 20% above with charity option).
- Business: Raise corporation tax threshold to £100k profits; cut main rate to 20% then 15% (year 3); abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax; simplify planning; reduce employment regulation; simplify the tax code.

NHS and social care:
- Zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS and social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; write off student fees pro‑rata over 10 years of NHS service; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; weekend theatres; better procurement; “Pharmacy First” approach; public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.
- Royal Commission on social care; close tax loopholes for offshore care‑home structures.

Energy and environment:
- Scrap Net Zero targets and related subsidies; fast‑track North Sea and shale; develop SMRs and other technologies.

Law, order, and justice:
- Recruit 40,000 police; increase stop and search; tougher sentences (including mandatory life for violent repeat offenders); expand prison capacity by 10,000 places; increase criminal justice budget to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; revise hate‑crime definitions; streamline policing, reduce paperwork.

Education:
- Curriculum review; restrict gender identity policies in schools; ensure single‑sex facilities and parental notification; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans and extend repayment; enforce entry standards; expand pupil referral units; promote 2‑year degrees.

Welfare and work:
- Incentivise work via higher tax threshold; target up to 2 million back to work; two‑strike rule on job offers; face‑to‑face assessments with exemptions for severe conditions.

Brexit and sovereignty:
- Scrap retained EU laws; abandon the Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate the Trade and Cooperation Agreement.

Defence and veterans:
- Raise defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by year 3 and 3% by year 6; pay review; legal protections; dedicated veterans department; recruit 30,000 for the army; reform procurement.

Housing:
- Fast‑track brownfield development; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility for landlords; strengthen leaseholder protections.

Infrastructure and transport:
- Cancel remaining HS2; repeal ULEZ/low‑traffic schemes; no bans on petrol/diesel; accelerate regional road/rail upgrades; new utility ownership model (50% public/50% UK pension funds); cap standing charges.

Agriculture and fisheries:
- Increase farm budget to £3bn; replace climate‑linked subsidies; tackle supermarket power; “Buy British” targets; cut red tape; restrict foreign fishing access; expand patrols; rebuild processing.

Constitution and governance:
- Leave the ECHR; reform the House of Lords and civil service leadership; restrict postal voting; consider PR via referendum; British Bill of Rights; overhaul equalities and free‑speech laws; reform the BBC funding model; new anti‑corruption unit; oppose WHO pandemic treaty and a CBDC; retain cash.

Funding summary (annualised):
- Claimed savings: ~£150bn plus £10bn from growth assumptions.
- Claimed costs: ~£141bn.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_E" | "TEXT_D"
}
